public_rationale: The funding total holds. OpenAI's $122 billion round plus Anthropic's $30 billion and $65 billion rounds come to $217 billion of announced capital in the nine months before the post. That counts commitments; about $35 billion of Amazon's share depends on future conditions. The "vast majority" part does not hold. Amazon and NVIDIA gave $80 billion to OpenAI. Microsoft's amount there can be at most $9 billion. Hyperscalers, Microsoft and NVIDIA account for at most $15 billion of each Anthropic round. Even at the most generous count, the four firms gave about $119 billion of $217 billion, roughly 55%. That is a majority, not a vast majority. The 70-80% share of AI revenue and compute demand could not be tested. No source measures it. Epoch AI's estimate that the two labs used 15-20% of installed compute at the end of 2025 is a different measure.
limitations: The four firms' share is an upper bound, because Microsoft's OpenAI amount is not disclosed.
"Vast majority" has no stated threshold; about 55% fails only under ordinary usage.
The share part is unresolved, not contradicted.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic account for 70–80% of all AI revenues and compute demand, funded by over $217 billion largely from Google, Amazon, Microsoft and NVIDIA in the last nine months.

statement.excerpt: Whenever more capacity comes online, it’s immediately sold to OpenAI or Anthropic, who make up anywhere from 70% to 80% of all AI revenues and compute demand, creating the illusion that revenue growth is “coming from demand for AI compute” rather than said demand coming from two companies that have been fed over $217 billion in the last nine months, with the vast majority of it coming from Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and NVIDIA themselves.

from_speaker: "Whenever more capacity comes online, it's immediately sold to OpenAI or Anthropic"
"who make up anywhere from 70% to 80% of all AI revenues and compute demand"
"two companies that have been fed over $217 billion in the last nine months"
"with the vast majority of it coming from Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and NVIDIA themselves"
our_interpretation: Tested as three parts: (a) OpenAI and Anthropic make up 70-80% of AI revenues and compute demand; (b) they received over $217B in the nine months before the post (about 2025-12-29 to 2026-09-29); (c) the vast majority of that came from Google, Amazon, Microsoft and NVIDIA.
For (b), "fed" is read as announced equity funding (committed capital) in that window.
For (c), "vast majority" is read in the ordinary sense: well over half, roughly two-thirds or more. A share near or below 55% is not a vast majority under any ordinary reading.
For (a), the present-tense share is read as of the post date. 'All AI revenues' has no named measure.
criteria.support_condition: (a) A credible measure puts the two labs at 70-80% of AI revenue or compute demand around September 2026; (b) announced funding to the two labs in the window totals about $217B or more; (c) Google, Amazon, Microsoft and NVIDIA supplied well over half of it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: (a) A credible measure puts their share well outside 70-80%; (b) funding in the window was well below $217B; (c) the four firms supplied about half or less.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI has closed its latest financing round with $122bn in committed capital, giving the AI company a post-money valuation of $852bn.
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's $122B round falls inside the nine-month window and is the largest part of the $217B total.

evidence.excerpt: We have raised $30 billion in Series G funding led by GIC and Coatue, valuing Anthropic at $380 billion post-money.
evidence.explanation: Anthropic's $30B Series G is inside the window. It was led by GIC and Coatue, not the four named firms, and includes only 'a portion' of Microsoft and NVIDIA's earlier commitments.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic has raised $65 billion in Series H funding led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, valuing the company at $965 billion post-money.
evidence.explanation: With e1 and e2, this gives $122B + $30B + $65B = $217B in the window, matching his total on a committed-capital basis.

evidence.excerpt: Amazon leads the round with a total investment commitment of $50bn, starting with $15bn and planning an additional $35bn subject to future conditions. Nvidia and SoftBank are each investing $30bn.
evidence.explanation: Upper bound on the four firms' share. In OpenAI's round, Amazon ($50B) and NVIDIA ($30B) plus at most $9B from Microsoft. In Anthropic's rounds, at most $15B each. That is at most $119B of $217B, about 55%. Not a vast majority.

evidence.excerpt: It also includes $15 billion of previously committed investments from hyperscalers, including $5 billion from Amazon.
evidence.explanation: Caps money from hyperscalers in the $65B Series H at $15B, an input to e4.

evidence.excerpt: NVIDIA and Microsoft will each invest up to $10 billion and $5 billion in Anthropic, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Caps the Microsoft/NVIDIA money in Series G at $15B, an input to e4.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic and OpenAI probably made up 15–20% of the world’s operational AI compute at the end of 2025.
evidence.locator: section 'What happens if frontier labs run out of headroom?', paragraph 1
evidence.explanation: A tentative estimate of the two labs' share of installed compute, far below 70-80%. It measures compute used, not new demand or revenue, and is from late 2025, so it does not settle part (a).

public_payload.what_would_resolve: For the share part: a credible market-wide measure of AI cloud revenue or new compute contracts by customer around September 2026. For the funding mix: disclosure of Microsoft's amount in OpenAI's round and Google's exact share of Series H.
